 :JUDGMENT:
This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 10.12.2016 wherein the petitioners have sought for compensation with respect to the death of Ramireddy @ Ramareddy due to the impact of the accident.
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.5675/2017 2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the son of deceased Ramireddy @ Ramareddy who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 10.12.2016 due to the negligence of the driver of the respondent's tractor vehicle.

It is submitted that on 10.12.2016 at about 6.00 p.m., deceased Ramireddy @
Ramareddy was proceeding in a Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-40-TA-6113 as an agricultural coolie (loader and unloader of mud) and when the tractor reached near Sakevandlapalli Devarakere village, Bagepalli taluk, at that time, driver of the said tractor drove in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, endangering human life,
due to rash driving Ramireddy fell down from the tractor and sustained severe injuries all over the body and succumbed to the injuries.

3. Consequently, on 11.12.2016 a FIR No.0311/2016 was registered with the Bagepalli Police station under Sec.279 and 304A of IPC and charge sheet was filed under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.181 of IMV Act.

sentences.text: 2 4. The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of tractor.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 39 years and working as an agricultural coolie and was earning Rs.500/- per day at the time of accident and he was the sole bread earner of the family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners have lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioners.

Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12%
p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
5. In pursuance of service of the notice issued, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their Counsels and filed Objections to the claim petition.

The Respondent No.1 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.1 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending tractor bearing chassis No.N8MB02467 and Engine No.N8MB02467.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.1 if any is subject to the validity of driving license SCCH 15 5 MVC No.5675/2017 and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Further mode of the accident and also involvement of the offending vehicle is denied.
The driver of the said tractor did not have valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

6. The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
It is submitted by the respondent No.2 that the alleged accident never took place due to the negligence on the part of this respondent.

Further submitted that this respondent has been driving the tractor by observing all the traffic rules and regulations with moderate speed and due to mechanical defect the said tractor suddenly stopped and as such this respondent has not driven the same in rash or negligent manner.
It is submitted that the offending vehicle is insured with respondent No.1.
It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant, SCCH 15 6 MVC No.5675/2017 excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

sentences.text: Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Ramareddy was died in RTA arising out of accident alleged to have been taken place on 10.12.2016 at about 6.00 p.m., at Sakevandlapalli village, Devarakere, Bagepalli taluk, CB pura district, due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-40-TA-6113?
2) Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the dependents of the deceased?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?

4 ) What Order or Award?
8.

In order to substantiate the claim petition, the claimants SCCH 15 7 MVC No.5675/2017 have examined petitioner No.1 as PW1 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 10 and the Respondent No.1 got examined one witness as RW.1 and relied upon Ex.R1 to 7.

Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly In the Affirmative Issue No.3 :
Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-40- TA-6113 (herein after referred to as offending vehicle).

11. In this regard PW.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and in SCCH 15 8 MVC No.5675/2017 her chief-examination she has deposed that on 10.12.2016 at around 6.00 p.m. her husband by name Ramireddy was proceeding in the Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-40-TA-6113 as agricultural coolie (loader and unloader of mud) and when the tractor came near Sakevandlapalli village, Bagepalli taluk, at that time all of a sudden the driver of the said tractor drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and as a result the deceased fell from the tractor and sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.
12.
The petitioner in support of her claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 documents.
Ex.P1 is the FIR registered against the driver of offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC on the basis of the complaint given by PW.1 on 11.12.2016.

In addition Ex.P2 and ExP3 Spot mahazar and sketch discloses that the accident has taken place in the lake compound and there is a 30 mtr thar road towards western side and towards southern side at distance of 20 mtr there is a Lakshmi Narasamma vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61724964/

sentences.text: In this regard the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has stated that the accident took place in the lake compound while taking mud and hence it is not road traffic accident.

However on perusal of the spot sketch and mahazar it discloses that either side of the spot of the accident there is road and the vehicle being a tractor it can be expected that it used for agricultural purpose and there are tyre marks of other vehicles in the spot of the accident which shows that said spot is used for movement of vehicles as a public place and hence it can be assumed that the spot of the accident is used for movement of vehicles and hence it can be concluded that it is road traffic accident.

13. In addition Ex.P7 - charge sheet discloses that the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and under sec.181 of IMV Act.

On perusal of the charge sheet discloses that the offending vehicle was proceeding from the road in order to fill mud and was going towards the lake compound from the road in a rash and negligent manner and the accident took place which goes to SCCH 15 10 MVC No.5675/2017 show that the offending vehicle was proceeding from the road towards the spot of the accident.
Hence, on the basis of Ex.P1 to 7 documents it can be satisfactorily concluded that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

14. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned, PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and in the cross-examination of PW.1 she has admitted that she has not seen the accident and came to know about the accident from the public and stated that she does not know where the accident took place.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent No.1.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.

The fact that the driver of the offending SCCH 15 11 MVC No.5675/2017 vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and under sec.181 of IMV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the death occurred in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that death occurred on account of rashness and negligence of driver, driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioners and in the 'Affirmative'.
15. Issue No.2:
It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased Ramireddy @ Ramareddy.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced Ex.P8 to 10 ration card and Aadhaar cards of the Petitioners.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased, they being the legal representatives of deceased Ramireddy @ Ramareddy have a right to apply for compensation.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Ramireddy @ Ramareddy and also they have proved that the death of Ramireddy @ Ramareddy has been caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for compensation.

However petitioner No.2 is major son and can earn on his own and maintain himself and hence he SCCH 15 13 MVC No.5675/2017 cannot be considered to be dependent on the income of the deceased though he could be entitled for compensation towards loss of estate and consortium.
Hence, petitioner No.1 is considered as the only dependent on the income of the deceased for the purpose of assessing compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 partly in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:

Computation of compensation under the various heads is assessed as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Age factor:
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 39 years.
In this regard, petitioners have not produced any document to prove the age of the deceased.
Hence, by considering Ex.P6 - PM report, the age of the deceased is taken as 45 years for the assessing compensation.
19. Income and avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was working as a coolie and was earning Rs.500/- per SCCH 15 14 MVC No.5675/2017 day.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.9,500/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 9,500X 12 = 1,14,000/-.

Hence for the purpose of computation of claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,14,000/-.
20.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

Relevant part of the judgment at paras 18- 19 is reproduced hereunder:
"18.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and Lakshmi Narasamma vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61724964/

sentences.text: (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."

Moving forward with the Issue of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
SCCH 15 16 MVC No.5675/2017 (i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.

sentences.text: Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 25% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the deceased is self - employed and was between 40 to 50 years.
21. At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his wife.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India was pleased to hold that where the sole dependent of family member,  of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
22. In this Petition, the deceased was aged 45 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 25% of the income has to be added.
So, 25% of Rs.9,500/- comes to Rs.2,375/-.

Therefore,
the income of the deceased comes to SCCH 15 17 MVC No.5675/2017 Rs.11,875/- p.m. (Rs.9,500/- +
Rs.2,375/- = Rs.11,875/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 14.

23. After deducting  of the income towards his personal expenses in Rs.11,875/- it comes to Rs.5,938/- (Rs.11,875/- - 5,937/-) and multiplier applied is 14, (Rs.5,938 x 12 = 71,256/-,
Rs.71,256/- x 14 = 9,97,584/-).

Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.9,97,584/-
towards loss of dependency.
24. Medical expenses: The petitioners have not produced any medical bills to show any expenses incurred in the hospital.
Hence the actual medical expenses incurred for the treatment of the deceased or any hospital charges are taken an Nil.
25. 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses'

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme SCCH 15 18 MVC No.5675/2017 Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads, namely, 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

27. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the SCCH 15 20 MVC No.5675/2017 conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KC-9330.

In this regard the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW.1.

Except denying that the driver of the SCCH 15 21 MVC No.5675/2017 offending vehicle was having driving license no evidence is adduced by the respondent No.2 to show that driver of the offending vehicle possessed valid driving license.
On the other hand respondent No.1 has produced the copy of insurance policy which is got marked as Ex.R3 which shows that is a package policy
however on perusal of ExR3 it discloses that there is only basis TP and paid driver cover and no additional premium was collected for loader and unloader.

Respondent No.1 has produced Ex.R1 which is the DL of respondent No.2 owner cum driver of the offending vehicle / tractor which shows that the date of issue of said DL is 02.02.2018 which is after the date of the accident and hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the respondent No.2 who is the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess valid DL.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".

sentences.text:
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.
Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.
33. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.11,30,684/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The claim petition filed by the petitioners against respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.
The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.11,30,684/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
SCCH 15 26 MVC No.5675/2017 The Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 95% to the Petitioner No.1 2) 5% to the petitioner No.2

After deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of E-payment after proper identification and the remaining 50% each of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However on perusal of the spot sketch and mahazar it discloses that either side of the spot of the accident there is road and the vehicle being a tractor it can be expected that it used for agricultural purpose and there are tyre marks of other vehicles in the spot of the accident which shows that said spot is used for movement of vehicles as a public place and hence it can be assumed that the spot of the accident is used for movement of vehicles and hence it can be concluded that it is road traffic accident.
Hence, on the basis of Ex.P1 to 7 documents it can be satisfactorily concluded that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent No.1.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
The fact that the driver of the offending SCCH 15 11 MVC No.5675/2017 vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and under sec.181 of IMV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the death occurred in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that death occurred on account of rashness and negligence of driver, driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased, they being the legal representatives of deceased Ramireddy @ Ramareddy have a right to apply for compensation.
As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Ramireddy @ Ramareddy and also they have proved that the death of Ramireddy @ Ramareddy has been caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for compensation.
The learned counsel for respondent No.1 has in support of his contention also relied on the following decisions:
SCCH 15 22 MVC No.5675/2017 2016 ACJ 823, between New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Mazo and others, wherein it observed as follows:
"Motor vehicles Act, 1988, Sec.147(1) Motor insurance - Tractor trailer - agricultural purpose - liability of insurance company - death of the deceased when a tractor - trailer driven rashly and negligently hit against him tribunal found that tractor-tailer was being used to transport stones from field to merely ditch and holding that vehicle was being used for agricultural purpose fastened liability on the insurance company - evidence that there was no agricultural field with so much quantity of stones in the area where the accident occurred - trailer did not have a registration number much less any insurance cover - whether tractor - trailer was used for commercial purpose and insurance company is exempted from liability - held: yes: only tractor owner is liable."
